**The Way of AI, grounded in practice (道).**

::: {.byline}
by [Chris Tham](https://christham.net)
:::

Anyone can open a chat window and get a fluent answer in seconds. Far fewer can
turn that fluency into work worth standing behind. We all draw on the same
frontier models, so the model was never the edge — **method is**. *AI-dō* is that
method: a structured, human-centred way of working with AI, earned task by task
and checked at every step.

It's a short, personal read — a candid, first-hand account of learning to get
dependable, worthwhile work from AI, with every claim grounded in a primary
source. It's meant to be read online — and it's yours to download too:

::: {.dl-buttons}
[Read Online](preface.qmd){.btn-dl .primary}
[Download PDF](ai-do.pdf){.btn-dl .ghost}
[Download ePub](ai-do.epub){.btn-dl .ghost}
:::

Start with the [Preface](preface.qmd), then follow the six-chapter climb from
personal productivity to software, to the disciplines that keep the work sound,
to responsibility, and finally to mastery.

::::
:::::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="html"}
*The Way of AI, grounded in practice (道)*

**愛 (ai)** — love: care for the people the work touches.
**道 (dō)** — the way: a craft refined over a lifetime.

*AI-dō* joins the two: human care and a practised craft. Read it as a path, not
a manual — the methods will change; the way of holding the work does not.
:::
